 ORDER

This appeal by the claimant under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 03.03.2020 passed by Ist Addl. MACT, Mandsaur in Claim Case No.231/2018 seeking enhancement of compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal.
2. The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.

As per the findings of the Tribunal,
for the death of Vijay, the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.10,78,000/- along with interest accepting earning of deceased as Rs.5,000/- per month.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant contended that compensation as awarded by the Tribunal accepting earning of deceased as Rs.5000/- per month is inadequate looking to the fact that deceased was supervisor in firm Patidar borewell and earning of Rs.11,500/ - per month which was certified by AW/3 Bhagatram be accepted.
So trial court committed error in not accepting per month income as Rs.11,500/- so prayed for accepting this appeal and enhancing the amount with adequate multiplier.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance comp any contended that claims tribunal rightly awarded compensation and argued in support of the findings recorded by the tribunal.
5.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that deceased was working as supervisor in Patidar borewell firm and earning Rs.11,500/- per month which is duly proved by the claimant's employer AW/3 Bhagatram, salary vouchers Ex.P/13 & 14, income tax return and computation sheets Ex.P/32 to 60 and attendance register Ex.P/16 to 30 and Ex.P/12 GST registration certificate of Patidar Borewell on record.

7. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent argued that salary certificate and pay slip of the deceased could not be proved before the tribunal and as such amount of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just, fair and reasonable and requires no interference by this Court.

8. In the case United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Shila Datta - 2011 ACJ 2729 (SC) apex Court has held as under:
16.

entities.text: United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Shila Datta - 2011 ACJ 2729 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the case of Shila Datta (Supra), this Court held as under :-
(5) A claim petition for compensation in regard to a motor accident (filed by the injured or in case of death, by the dependant family members) before the Motor Accident Claims Learned Tribunal constituted under Section 165 of the Act is neither a suit nor an adversarial lis in the traditional sense.
It is a proceeding in terms of and regulated by the provisions of Chapter XII of the Act which is a complete Code in itself.
We may in this context refer to the following significant aspects in regard to the Learned Tribunals and determination of compensation by Learned Tribunals: ...
Xxx xxx xxx (ii)The rules of pleadings do not strictly apply as the claimant is required to make an application in a form prescribed under the Act.
In fact, there is no pleading where the proceedings are suo moto initiated by the Learned Tribunal.

...
Xxx xxx xxx (vi) The Learned Tribunal is required to follow such summary procedure as it thinks fit.

It may choose one or more persons possessing special knowledge of and matters relevant to inquiry, to the assist it in holding the enquiry (vide Section 169 of the Act)."
17.

Reference in this connection may also be made to the observations made by this Court in the case of Sunita & Ors. Vs. Rajasthan State Road Transport Corporation & Ors.4 , wherein it was observed as under :-
(20) "It is thus well settled that in motor accident claim cases, once the foundational fact, namely, the actual occurrence of the accident, has been established, then the Smt. Rakhi vs Sunil on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195848710/
4

entities.text: Sunita & Ors. Vs. Rajasthan State Road Transport Corporation & Ors.4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Tribunal's role would be to calculate the quantum of just compensation if the accident had taken place by reason of negligence of the driver of a motor vehicle and,
while doing so, the Tribunal would not be strictly bound by the pleadings of the parties.

Notably, while deciding cases arising out of motor vehicle accidents, the standard of proof to be borne in mind must be of preponderance of 4 (2020) 13 SCC 486 8 probability and not the strict standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt which is followed in criminal cases."
18.

Similarly, in the case of Kusum Lata & Ors. Vs. Satbir & Ors.5 , this Court observed that it is well known that in a case relating to motor accident claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case as it is required to be done in a criminal trial.

entities.text: Kusum Lata & Ors. Vs. Satbir & Ors.5
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Court must keep this distinction in mind.

19. It is well settled that Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is a beneficial piece of legislation and as such,
while dealing with compensation cases, once the actual occurrence of the accident has been established, the Tribunal's role would be to award just and fair compensation.

As held by this Court in Sunita (Supra) and Kusum Lata (Supra), strict rules of evidence as applicable in a criminal trial,
are not applicable in motor accident compensation cases, i.e., to say, "the standard of proof to be borne in mind must be of preponderance of probability and not the strict standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt which is followed in criminal cases".

9. In view of the above observations held by the apex Court and perusal of the record of the trial court it was found that AW/3 Bhagatram who is the prioprietor of the Patidar firm stated in examination in chief that his firm was registered and online GST registration is Ex.P/12, he is income tax payee and his return for the year 2018-19 is Ex.P/13, computation sheet is Ex.P/14 and firm's profit and loss account is Ex.P/15.
He further stated in examination in chief that deceased was working as supervisor in his firm.
His initial pay was Rs.10,000/- per month and at the time of accident his pay was Rs.11500/- per month.

His attendance register is Ex.P/16 to 30, salary vouchers Ex.P/13 & 14, Income tax return and computation sheets Ex.P/32 to 60.
10.
This witness AW/3 Bhagatram is intact in his cross examination so there is no reason to disbelieve his evidence.
So considering the evidence of AW/3 in the considered opinion of this Court trial court has committed error in not accepting salary certificate of the deceased.
So document was duly proved by the AW/3 and corroborated by the evidence of claimant.
So as such trial Court has not justified in assessing the income of the deceased at Rs.5000/- per month at the relevant time.
So finding in this regard of the tribunal is set aside and this court hold the income of the deceased at the time of accident as Rs.11500/-.

So annual income of the deceased is Rs.11500 x 12=138000/-.
11.
As far as age of the deceased is concerned according to the driving license of the deceased Ex.P/10c, date of birth of deceased was 25.01.1983 so he was aged 35 years at the time of accident.

However, award of future prospects at the rate of 40% needs to be added in view of law laid down by the apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and others - 2017 ACJ 2700.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and others - 2017 ACJ 2700
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So annual income plus future prospects is Rs.138000+55200= 193200.

5 12.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the decision in the case of Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another- (2009) 6 SCC 121, 1/3 amount should be deducted towards deceased's personal expenses if less than three persons are dependent on him.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another- (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case, there are more than 4 persons dependent upon deceased so 1/4 amount must be deducted for personal expenses so in this regard tribunal has rightly deducted  amount for personal expenses.
As per Sarla Verma's case deceased was 32-35 years age so multiplier in this case is 13.
Deceased left behind him 5 dependents i.e. present appellants.
In view of this amount of Rs.40,000/- awarded by the tribunal is insufficient in my view and deserves to be enhanced.

In the case of United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur - 2020 ACJ 2131 apex Court has awarded loss of spousal consortium at the rate of Rs.40000/- and for loss of parental consortium each child at the rate of Rs.40,000/-.

entities.text: United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur - 2020 ACJ 2131
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This head also needs to be increased to 10% after every 3 years.
Accordingly amount of Rs.40000/- towards consortium is increased to Rs.44000/- to each child amounting to total of Rs.2,20000/-.
Along with this Rs.15000/- each under the head of funeral expenses and loss of estate is awarded.

14. Hence, total compensation payable to the appellants under various heads is ascertained by this court as under:
Loss of dependency -Rs.138000+40% FP x 12 -  personal expenses x 16=23,18,400/-
 Loss of consortium -Rs.2,20,000/-
 Funeral expenses -Rs.15,000/-
 Loss of estate -Rs.15,000/-
 ----------------------
 TOTAL Rs.25,68,400/-
15.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.25,68,400/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.10,78,000/-.

Accordingly,
the appellants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs.14,90,400/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
16. In the result, the appeal is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.14,90,400/-.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.

17. The appellants have valued the appeal only to the extent of Rs.10 lakhs and paid the Court fee accordingly, however, for the remaining amount the Court fee shall be paid by the appellants within Smt. Rakhi vs Sunil on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195848710/
6 a period of one month and thereafter the amount shall be released by the Insurance Company on receiving the certificate.
